threads.body: The filtering wrapper does not override `Meter.batchCallback(...)`. The interface default creates a no-op callback instead of delegating to this wrapper's underlying meter, so handlers that use batch callbacks never collect even included metrics. `CassandraCompactionProgressHandler` does this at lines 87–95. The wrapper needs batch-callback handling that preserves filtering, including the case where a handler's measurements are split between included and excluded names.

When a handler's metrics are all excluded, each observable measurement comes from the no-op meter, but this still delegates them to the real SDK meter. The SDK discards measurements not created by that meter and then rejects the empty batch with `IllegalStateException("Callback with no instruments is not allowed")`, so `JmxTelemetry.start()` fails instead of simply suppressing the handler's metrics. Handle the all-filtered case without registering a real batch callback, while preserving delegation for any included measurements.

threads.body: These lookups resolve to `otel.instrumentation.jmx.metrics.included` and `.excluded` under the flat configuration bridge, not the documented `otel.jmx.*` properties. The existing JMX keys require explicit entries in `ConfigPropertiesBackedDeclarativeConfigProperties.SPECIAL_MAPPINGS`; without matching entries here, both newly documented system properties/environment variables are silently ignored. Add the two bridge mappings (plus coverage) for `java.jmx.metrics.included/excluded` to the advertised flat keys.

This now presents concrete, copyable code but does not import `GlobalOpenTelemetry` or the newly used `IncludeExclude` (and the snippet also uses `Paths`). Add those imports so the documented example compiles.

[Documentation] These new public configuration properties are absent from `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/metadata.yaml`. That file feeds the generated instrumentation/configuration references, so both supported filters remain missing from `docs/instrumentation-list.yaml` and the declarative configuration catalog. Add list-valued metadata entries for `otel.jmx.metrics.included` and `.excluded` with their `java.jmx.metrics.*` declarative names.

The metadata now advertises `otel.instrumentation.jmx.enabled`, but the non-v3 installer still reads `config.getBoolean("enabled", true)` and the bridge explicitly maps `java.jmx.enabled` to `otel.jmx.enabled` (`ConfigPropertiesBackedDeclarativeConfigProperties.java:101`). As a result, the generated configuration reference tells standard-mode users to set a property that this installer ignores. Keep the existing name until the installer/bridge migration is implemented together.
